BIC for multiple Gaussian graphical models

Source: R/loss.R
ggm_bic.Rd

A BIC-type criterion for tuning joint estimators of K precision matrices (e.g. the penalties of the joint graphical lasso), summed over groups: $$\sum_k \left[\mathrm{tr}(S_k\hat\Theta_k) - \log|\hat\Theta_k| + \frac{\log n_k}{n_k} E_k\right],$$ where \(S_k\) is the sample covariance of group \(k\) (denominator \(n_k - 1\)), \(n_k\) its sample size and \(E_k\) the number of entries of \(\hat\Theta_k\) with \(|\hat\theta_{ij}| \ge\) threshold. \(E_k\) counts every such entry of the matrix, including the diagonal and both triangles. This is the per-observation form used in the Koyejo lab joint graphical lasso code (vBIC()); smaller is better.

Usage

ggm_bic(data_list, theta_list, threshold = 0.001)

Arguments

data_list

List of K data matrices (\(n_k\) x p).

theta_list

List of K estimated p x p precision matrices.

threshold

Entries with absolute value >= threshold count as non-zero. Default 0.001.

Value

A number; NA if any \(\hat\Theta_k\) has missing values or a zero or negative determinant, or the data have missing values.

References

Danaher, P., Wang, P. & Witten, D.M. (2014). The joint graphical lasso for inverse covariance estimation across multiple classes. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 76(2), 373-397.

Examples

set.seed(1)
X <- list(matrix(rnorm(100), 25, 4), matrix(rnorm(80), 20, 4))
theta <- lapply(X, function(x) solve(cov(x)))
ggm_bic(X, theta)
#> [1] 10.12662
